title: Is it really talking to Azure SQL?
scenario: "The smoke test is green, but the product list looks like demo data. Prove the API reads from Azure SQL with its managed identity — no passwords." — QA lead
mission: Wire workload identity end to end and prove the database path with evidence the smoke test alone does not give.
objectives: Trace SA annotation → federated credential → managed identity → SQL user
Grant the identity in SQL with the script

prerequisites.notes: GitOps bootstrapped (C012) or the chart deployed by Argo CD.

steps.title: Follow the chain
steps.detail: List the federated credentials of the API identity and compare subjects with the service accounts.
steps.command: az identity federated-credential list -g rg-mfs-portal-lab --identity-name <api-identity> -o table

steps.title: Grant SQL access
steps.detail: Create the contained user for the managed identity.

steps.title: Prove the data source
steps.detail: Read /readyz through the API server service proxy (no exec, no port-forward needed).

criteria.text: A federated credential exists for each portal namespace
The API service account carries the workload identity client id
/readyz reports database: sql in dev and prod

expectedResult: Evidence that the API reads from Azure SQL, not the in-memory fallback.
recovery: Login failed for user <token-identified principal>: the SQL user is missing — run the grant script again.
dont: Do not create a SQL login with a password
Do not trust a green smoke test as proof of the database path
hints: Four links: service account annotation, pod label, federated credential subject, SQL user.
/readyz returns the database mode the API is using.

interview.question: Explain workload identity on AKS and how the pod gets a token for Azure SQL.
followUps: Why is a passing smoke test not proof of the integration?

debrief: The kubelet projects a service-account token; the webhook injects AZURE_FEDERATED_TOKEN_FILE; Entra exchanges it (subject match) for a managed-identity token; SQL maps it to a contained user. The smoke test checks /api/products returns 200, which the in-memory catalog also satisfies — /readyz database mode is the real proof.

checker.plan: Read-only: az identity federated-credential list, kubectl get sa -o json, kubectl get --raw service proxy /readyz.

validation.notes: Checker not implemented yet; needs a running cluster.
